TYPED: Maths twice a week for Grade 1.
WHY: 'Twice a week' vs 'twice a day': Periods per week is setup data, not max_subject_periods_per_day.
RIGHT HANDLING: Map to setup requirement or ask

TYPED: Priya should have less than 28 periods.
WHY: 'Less than' vs 'no more than': Less than 28 = max 27; no more than 28 = max 28.

TYPED: Don't put PE right before Maths.
WHY: 'After PE' direction: Same as Maths can't follow PE: first=PE, second=Maths.

TYPED: Maths and PE shouldn't be next to each other.
WHY: 'Next to each other' is symmetric: Forbids both orders.

TYPED: No double English.
WHY: Same subject back to back: One subject, consecutive -> max_consecutive_periods=1, not min_gap.

TYPED: Library in the 8th period.
WHY: 'Last period' depends on the day: 8th is only 'last' if the day has 8 periods (Saturday may have 4).
RIGHT HANDLING: Prefer position=last only if they said last

TYPED: Mrs. Rao doesn't work weekends.
WHY: 'Weekend': Only days the school runs matter (usually Saturday).

TYPED: Maths only in the morning.
WHY: 'Morning' / 'afternoon': Needs the break position to know where morning ends.

TYPED: CS on Monday for Grade 6.
WHY: 'CS' abbreviation: Computer Science or Communication Skills? SST vs Social Science too.

TYPED: KS sir off Friday.
WHY: Titles and nicknames: Initials may match 2 teachers.

TYPED: 8th has Maths first.
WHY: Grade vs section: All of Grade 8 or only one section?

TYPED: Juniors don't have PE first period.
WHY: Group words: Juniors = which grades? Varies by school.

TYPED: Arjun only comes on Monday.
WHY: 'Only' flips meaning: Means unavailable on every other day, not available on Monday.

TYPED: It's not that PE can't be on Friday.
WHY: Double negative: Means PE is allowed on Friday - no rule.

TYPED: Mr. Khan has lab duty, so he's busy.
WHY: Reason sounds like a rule: When? Missing day/period.

TYPED: Try to keep Maths first.
WHY: Soft vs hard: 'Try' means soft, can be broken.

TYPED: No PE Friday and Maths first for 10.
WHY: Two rules, one sentence: Two constraints with different scopes.

TYPED: No PE Friday - no wait, Thursday.
WHY: Correction: Keep only the corrected day.

TYPED: Can we not have PE on Friday?
WHY: Question that's a rule: It's a request, not a real question.

TYPED: Can Mrs. Rao take 8 periods Monday?
WHY: Real question: Not a rule.

TYPED: Max 30 periods.
WHY: Per-teacher vs school-wide cap: For one teacher or for every teacher?
RIGHT HANDLING: Ask if no name given and context unclear

TYPED: Priya max 20 hours a week.
WHY: Hours vs periods: Periods are often 40 min, so 20 hours is about 30 periods.

TYPED: Maths first every day / no Maths first on Monday.
WHY: Contradiction: Both can't hold.

TYPED: Make the timetable balanced and nice for everyone
WHY: Not specific enough to enforce

TYPED: Mr. Verma can't come on Tuesday (no Mr. Verma on staff)
WHY: Refers to a teacher/subject/class that doesn't exist in setup
RIGHT HANDLING: Return null for the teacher and ask which teacher is meant; don't guess

TYPED: all 10th sections maths same time, rao mam will take all 4
WHY: Putting 4 sections in one slot needs 4 Maths teachers at once. The rule is only impossible in combination with the setup data (one teacher for all four).
RIGHT HANDLING: Flag the clash with setup; ask whether to combine the sections in the hall or assign more teachers

TYPED: Priya ma'am only comes MWF, but needs 30 periods a week
WHY: 3 days x 8 periods = 24 slots at most, so 30 periods cannot fit. Availability and load are each valid alone; the arithmetic between them is not.
RIGHT HANDLING: Flag the capacity gap and ask which rule gives way

TYPED: 9A PE on mon means art also mon. no art on mondays for 9A. and 9A PE has to be every day
WHY: PE daily forces PE on Monday, which forces Art on Monday, which is banned. Any two rules are fine; only the chain of three fails.
RIGHT HANDLING: Report all three rules together, not just the last one entered

TYPED: teacher availability more imp than subject order, subject order more imp than maths first rule, maths first more imp than teacher availability
WHY: The priority ranking is a cycle, so no consistent order exists (extends C089).
RIGHT HANDLING: Ask which link in the cycle to drop

TYPED: Give Mr. Khan some good classes this year so he doesn't quit
WHY: Good classes has no measurable meaning (better-behaved, senior, fewer periods, fewer last periods?), and the reason is not a rule.
RIGHT HANDLING: Ask what makes a class good and turn the answer into an assignment or load rule

TYPED: only 12th can use physics lab in the afternoon
WHY: Either afternoons are reserved for Grade 12 (others use mornings), or Grade 12 may use the lab only in afternoons. The two readings block opposite groups.

TYPED: Grade 8 needs no free period on Friday
WHY: Unclear whether every Grade 8 section or one section is meant, and whether Library, Clubs or activity periods count as free periods.
RIGHT HANDLING: Confirm the scope and ask what counts as a free period
